poll_basis: mean of 2 polls: Ipsos Markinor (ANC 64.7, DA 10.8; 9.1% unsure excluded and renormalised) and Plus 94 (ANC 60, DA 16; as reported)
notes: National Assembly ballot. results_known = 23 Apr 2009, when partial IEC results showed ANC victory in sight (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2009/4/23/anc-nears-s-africa-election-win); IEC final results 25 Apr 2009 (sanews). Markinor fieldwork was early March 2009 (Politicsweb 15 Apr) and Plus 94 fieldwork date not reported; poll_date is the Wikinews publication date. Wikinews gives Markinor undecided 4.2% + refused 3.9%, Politicsweb gives 9.1% unsure; Politicsweb figure used. No Wikipedia poll table exists for 2009. Polls are old/sparse - low confidence. market_preferred left blank: no clear-cut financial-press framing found (ANC win never in doubt).

poll_basis: final Ipsos/Sunday Times poll (Apr 2014, published 4 May 2014); undecided already allocated by pollster (no DK share reported)
notes: National Assembly ballot. results_known = 8 May 2014, ANC lead clear from IEC results board (https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2014/5/8/south-africas-ruling-anc-takes-election-lead); IEC final results 10 May 2014. Only Ipsos published a regular series in the final weeks (a DA-internal Greenberg poll, ANC 59/DA 26, excluded as partisan). Wikipedia notes the final Ipsos wave was based on 500 interviews on 23 Apr 2014. market_preferred blank: no clear-cut framing found.

poll_basis: mean of last poll by each main pollster: IRR 18-25 Apr (ANC 49.5, DA 21.3, DK 0.9) and Ipsos 22 Mar-17 Apr (ANC 56.9, DA 15.2, DK 12.5); each normalised excl. don't know
market_preferred_note: Investors wanted a strong ANC (Ramaphosa) mandate; weak ANC/coalitions seen as rand-negative: https://businesstech.co.za/news/government/314974/why-investors-want-a-big-win-for-the-anc/
notes: National Assembly ballot. results_known = 10 May 2019 (75% of districts declared, ANC 57.2%: https://businesstech.co.za/news/?p=315956); IEC declared final results 11 May 2019. Excluded Intellidex 2 May 'investor poll' (survey of investors' expectations, not voters). Coding: for SA, 'a' = strong ANC share (reform-wing Ramaphosa mandate), the financial-press framing in 2019.

poll_basis: mean of last poll by each pollster with fieldwork in final week: AtlasIntel 25-28 May, Social Research Foundation 27 May, Afrobarometer 22 May; shares as published (no DK column)
market_preferred_note: Not a/b-codable: markets favoured an ANC-DA (or ANC+MPC) coalition over ANC-EFF/MK; see https://poundsterlinglive.com/zar/20372-south-african-rand-rallies-investors-spy-potential-anc-da-coalition
notes: National Assembly ballot. ANC won plurality but lost its majority (40.18%) -> GNU with DA. results_known = 31 May 2024, when partial IEC count put ANC clearly below 50% (https://www.aljazeera.com/amp/news/liveblog/2024/5/31/south-africa-election-results-live-early-results-put-anc-short-of-majority); Reuters flagged likely loss of majority on 30 May; IEC declared final results 2 Jun 2024. Poll leader/winner by plurality = ANC, but the market-relevant outcome was ANC<50% and coalition partner choice; coding left blank deliberately. Afrobarometer 'others' column (22%) may contain undecided - not normalised (not separable).

poll_basis: single final poll listed: VERSO June 2007 (CHP incl. DSP joint list); undecided treatment not stated by source
market_preferred_note: ISE hit all-time peak and lira a six-year high after AKP's win (single-party govt, no coalition): https://hedgeco.net/news/08/2007/brighter-times-for-turkey.html
notes: poll_date month-only (VERSO June 2007, via Angus Reid as cited on Wikipedia). Sparse/old polling; the VERSO shares sum to ~79% so likely include undecided/unallocated - low confidence, not normalised because the denominator is unknown. Market coding from ex-post reaction (stocks/lira rallied on AKP majority).

poll_basis: no numeric pre-referendum poll found (Wikipedia cites only a mid-July Angus Reid poll showing a 'vast majority' in favour, no figures)
notes: Direct election of the president. Yes ranked a on the qualitative Angus Reid description (no numbers). Actual shares computed from YSK valid votes (yes 19,422,714 / no 8,744,947) as given on Wikipedia.

poll_basis: mean of final national forecasts by A&G (AKP 43-46, CHP 25-26), Anar (AKP 43-46, CHP 24-26) and Pollmark (AKP ~48, CHP ~23); range midpoints used
notes: Actual = national provincial-assembly (il genel meclisi) vote share. Forecasts are pollster-director statements reported by Timeturk (fieldwork dates not given; Pollmark explicitly for provincial council vote). Large polling miss (AKP overestimated ~7pp). No Wikipedia poll table exists. market_preferred blank (no clear-cut framing found).

poll_basis: final KONDA poll (Sep 2010; Yes 56.8, No 25.6, undecided 17.6) normalised excl. undecided
market_preferred_note: Reuters 7 Sep 2010: 'Markets may turn negative if the constitutional changes are rejected': https://investing.com/news/forex-news/refile-turkey-markets-weaker,-cautious-ahead-of-referendum-158527
notes: poll_date = publication date of KONDA poll (Al Jazeera, 11 Sep 2010, as cited on Wikipedia). Only other poll found (SONAR, Aug 2010: Yes 49.1/No 50.9) is a month earlier and not included. Actual computed from infobox yes/no counts (the page's results template has slightly different counts, 21,788,272/15,855,041 - same shares to 2dp: 57.88/42.12).

poll_basis: mean of the three May 2011 polls listed: ORC 20 May (49.5/25.2), Andy-Ar May (52/27), Konsensus May (48.6/28.3); shares as published
market_preferred_note: Investors initially called AKP majority short of the 330-seat referendum threshold an 'ideal scenario': https://www.brecorder.com/news/amp/18467
notes: Andy-Ar and Konsensus rows dated only 'May 2011'; poll_date = latest exact date (ORC). Market preference was specifically AKP single-party majority without a constitution-changing supermajority.

poll_basis: mean of final nationwide polls by Konda (22-23 Mar; 46/27), Gezici (~10 days before vote; 46.2/27.2) and ORC (45.7/28.3) as reported by Diken
notes: Actual = national municipal-councillor vote share (Wikipedia's headline basis for 2014; provincial assemblies were abolished in metropolitan provinces in 2014, so not strictly comparable with the 2009 provincial-assembly basis). AKP declared victory in the early hours of 31 Mar. ORC fieldwork date not stated. market_preferred blank (no clear-cut framing found).

poll_basis: mean of last poll by each of 10 pollsters dated 20 Jul-8 Aug 2014 (Andy-Ar, A&G, Konda, Paradigma, SONAR, Ajans Press, ORC, TUSIAR, Gezici, Optimar), each rescaled so the 3 candidates sum to 100
notes: First direct presidential election; won in round 1 (no run-off). Poll dates in the Wikipedia table appear to be publication dates. CHP-commissioned poll excluded. market_preferred blank (no clear-cut framing found).

poll_basis: mean of last poll by each of 14 pollsters with fieldwork ending 17 May-2 Jun 2015 (incl. 3 released after the 28 May poll ban); shares as published (decided voters)
market_preferred_note: 'least bad outcome for the markets would be an outright AKP majority government' (5 Jun 2015): https://hurriyetdailynews.com/markets-await-uncertain-turkish-election-outcome-83548
notes: AKP won plurality but lost its majority (hung parliament -> Nov 2015 snap election); lira hit record low next day. Gezici, ORC, Konda final polls were released after the polling ban (flagged on Wikipedia). Actual includes diaspora votes (domestic-only: AKP 40.7, CHP 25.1).

poll_basis: mean of last poll by each of 15 pollsters with fieldwork ending 15-29 Oct 2015; shares as published (decided voters)
market_preferred_note: Coface: 'the single-party government was the most market-friendly outcome': https://www.gtreview.com/news/europe/turkey-akp-victory-relieves-market-tensions/
notes: AKP regained single-party majority, large polling miss (~+6.6pp vs polls); lira +4-5% next day.

poll_basis: mean of last poll by each of 11 pollsters with fieldwork ending 4-13 Apr 2017, using Wikipedia's Yes/No-only (excl. undecided) columns; CHP-commissioned polls excluded
market_preferred_note: Bloomberg: 'Most money managers see a no vote as more destabilising for markets' (yes = temporary relief): https://www.gulf-times.com/story/544421/investors-just-want-referendum-done-with-in-turkey-scenarios/amp
notes: Executive presidency. Opposition contested the result (unstamped ballots accepted by YSK). Market preference for Yes was relative/short-term (many analysts flagged long-run institutional concerns).

poll_basis: presidential race: mean of last poll by each of 6 pollsters with fieldwork ending 3-17 Jun 2018 (Gezici, Plus Mayak, AKAM, REMRES, Mediar, MAK), each rescaled so 6 candidates sum to 100; party-commissioned (CHP, IYI) polls excluded
notes: Same-day presidential + parliamentary; cand_a/b are the presidential candidates. Erdogan won outright in round 1 (no run-off); People's Alliance won parliamentary majority. market_preferred blank: pre-vote coverage was mixed (lira rallied ~3% on the decisive result, but analysts expected the bounce to fade on central-bank independence concerns), not a clear-cut a/b preference.

poll_basis: single latest nationwide poll listed: Konsensus 26 Feb 2019 (~5 weeks before vote; shares as published)
notes: Actual = national municipal-council vote share (Wikipedia infobox basis). AKP (People's Alliance) won the national vote but CHP won Ankara and Istanbul (Istanbul later annulled -> 23 Jun re-run). Only one nationwide poll in the final 2 months - weak poll basis. market_preferred blank (no clear-cut framing found).

poll_basis: mean of last poll by each of 11 pollsters with fieldwork ending 11-20 Jun 2019, each rescaled to candidates incl. 'other' (undecided and not-voting excluded)
notes: NOT nationwide: single-city re-run of the annulled 31 Mar 2019 Istanbul mayoral vote, coded local_nationwide per study convention because of its market relevance. Yildirim conceded the same evening. market_preferred blank (no clear-cut framing found).

poll_basis: POLITICO Europe Poll of Polls (presidential, last update 12 May 2023; integer-rounded); Euronews average 12 May: Kilicdaroglu 48.9, Erdogan 45.8
odds_basis: Smarkets price for Kilicdaroglu/opposition winning the presidency (overall contest, not round 1), single side reported, not overround-adjusted; same source: Polymarket 0.67, Metaculus 0.60
market_preferred_note: Markets/investors favoured an opposition win and return to orthodox policy (Reuters, 12 May 2023): https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2023-05-12/rpt-investors-buckle-pivotal-turkey-elections
notes: Round 1 of presidential + same-day parliamentary vote; cand_a/b are presidential candidates. Poll leader (Kilicdaroglu) trailed: no candidate >50% -> run-off 28 May. Actual shares computed from YSK round-1 valid votes on Wikipedia (Erdogan 27,133,849; Kilicdaroglu 24,595,178; Ogan 2,831,239; Ince 235,783). Ince withdrew 11 May but stayed on ballot. Gambling.com (pre-R1 exchange prices, undated) had Kilicdaroglu 1.62 vs Erdogan 2.2 -> 0.576 normalised.

poll_basis: POLITICO Europe Poll of Polls for the run-off (last update 28 May 2023; integer-rounded)
odds_basis: exchange betting sites as reported by Gambling.com: Erdogan 1.14, Kilicdaroglu 6.5 (decimal); normalised for overround
market_preferred_note: Same framing as round 1: investors preferred Kilicdaroglu/orthodox policy (Erdogan's first-round lead hit lira/bonds): https://www.kitco.com/news/off-the-wire/2023-05-12/rpt-investors-buckle-pivotal-turkey-elections
notes: Run-off. POLITICO aggregate 'last updated 28 May' per Wikipedia. odds_date = article last-updated date. Official national total (no diaspora split).

poll_basis: no verifiable final nationwide local-vote poll found (Wikipedia lists only city-level polls); poll columns left blank
notes: Actual = national municipal-councillor vote share (Wikipedia/YSK). Without a verified final nationwide poll, cand_a=AKP is assigned as the incumbent national leader (AKP led the 2019 local vote 42.56 vs 29.36) - this ordering is NOT poll-based; margin negative because CHP came first (first CHP national win since 1977). market_preferred blank (no clear-cut framing found).

poll_basis: no verifiable final national party poll with figures found (LSI's final survey release of 7 Apr 2009 gave no party shares); poll columns blank
market_preferred_note: Reuters scenarios (7 Apr 2009): strong Democrat showing -> rupiah firms, stocks bounce; Golkar/PDI-P coalition = worst case: https://investing.com/news/forex-news/scenarios-possible-investment-outcomes-from-indonesia's-polls-43127
notes: cand ordering a=PD, b=Golkar is NOT from a verified poll (the only figured poll found, LRI Feb 2009, had Golkar 20.1 > PD 15.5 > PDI-P 15.3 two months out); it follows the actual top two. KPU certified results 9 May 2009; quick counts on vote day. Wikipedia 2009 page gives PD 20.81 (votes 21,655,295); the 2014 page's comparison row gives 20.85 - small source discrepancy.

poll_basis: final LSI (Lembaga Survei Indonesia) survey 30 Jun-3 Jul 2009, n=3000 (SBY 63.1, Megawati 19.6, Kalla 10.6), normalised to the three candidates (6.7% residual treated as undecided)
market_preferred_note: Reuters scenarios (7 Jul 2009): decisive SBY first-round win could spark 10-15% rally; SBY loss = worst case: https://investing.com/news/forex-news/scenarios-possible-market-impacts-from-indonesian-polls-69279
notes: No run-off: SBY won >50% in round 1 (quick counts same day; KPU declared 23 Jul 2009). Single poll only; Jakarta Post (8 Jul) notes this LSI survey was funded by Fox Indonesia, SBY's party consultant - possible house effect.

poll_basis: mean of polls with fieldwork ending in final 3 weeks: Roy Morgan 16-30 Mar (PDI-P 37, Golkar 17) and JSI 24-30 Mar (24.7, 18.0); both report no undecided
market_preferred_note: 'Jokowi effect': markets wanted a strong PDI-P result; JCI fell 3.3% when PDI-P underperformed: https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2014/04/14/why-market-disappointed-with-election-results
notes: Quick counts on vote day. Only two polls in the final 3 weeks, with very different PDI-P levels (37 vs 24.7) - high uncertainty; both overstated PDI-P.

poll_basis: mean of final surveys reported by Jakarta Post 8 Jul 2014: LSI (Lingkaran) 2-5 Jul (47.8/44.2, 8% undecided) and PolMark 24-28 Jun (44.6/41.0); each normalised to the two candidates
market_preferred_note: Morgan Stanley: Prabowo win would trigger outflows; Deutsche Bank survey: 56% would sell on Prabowo vs 6% on Jokowi: https://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2014/06/28/prabowo-victory-bad-business-global-bankers
notes: Two-candidate race, so no run-off possible. Both camps claimed victory on quick-count night; most credible quick counts showed Jokowi ~52-53% the same afternoon, KPU declared 22 Jul 2014 (Prabowo rejected the result).

poll_basis: mean of polls with fieldwork ending in final 3 weeks: Charta Politika 5-10 Apr (55.7/38.8) and SMRC 5-8 Apr (56.8/37.0), each normalised to the two candidates
market_preferred_note: Stocks/rupiah climbed on Jokowi win; Morgan Stanley: 'time to brush aside tail risk concerns and buy Indonesian equities': https://gulfnews.com/business/markets/indonesian-stocks-rupiah-climb-as-jokowi-wins-second-term-1.63412303
notes: Simultaneous presidential + legislative; cand_a/b = presidential tickets (legislative: PDI-P 19.33%). Two-candidate race, no run-off. LSI 18-26 Mar (60/40) falls just outside the 3-week window and is excluded. Market coding partly ex post.

poll_basis: mean of last poll by each of 8 pollsters with fieldwork ending 25 Jan-8 Feb 2024 (SPIN, LSI Denny JA, LSI, Indikator, Populi, Poltracking, Point Indonesia, Political Weather Station), each rescaled so 3 candidates sum to 100
market_preferred_note: Markets welcomed likely one-round Prabowo win (removed run-off uncertainty, continuity), with fiscal caveats: https://www.businessday.co.za/bd/world/asia/2024-02-15-markets-welcome-likely-prabowo-victory-in-indonesian-elections/
notes: Simultaneous presidential + legislative; cand_a/b = presidential tickets. Key market question was whether Prabowo cleared 50% to avoid a June run-off - he did (no run-off). Polymarket ran a 'Prabowo wins?' market but no verifiable pre-vote price was found. Market coding 'a' is moderate (rupiah/bonds muted; fiscal concerns).
